churn_resistance.rationale: A framework or API upgrade would touch very few files (config, the one data module, current page syntax), and no internals or undocumented behaviour are relied on; the drag is the pervasive `any` at the API boundary and the duplicated client-navigation script, which make the *data* and the *second* copy of that script the churn risks.

findings.issue: Reads process.env.API_BASE_URL directly at module scope; Astro's environment-variables docs (astro:env, stable since 5.0) explicitly recommend getSecret() from astro:env/server instead, so this is the one legacy-era pattern in the app
findings.suggestion: Declare an astro.config env schema ({ API_BASE_URL: { type: 'string', context: 'server' } }) and import it (or getSecret('API_BASE_URL')), gaining validation and adapter portability

findings.issue: Near-duplicate client-side partial-navigation code (AbortController + fetch + DOMParser + swap) copied from app/src/pages/index.astro:124-136; two copies will drift (they already differ: innerHTML vs replaceWith)
findings.suggestion: Extract a shared lib/partials.ts module (exported via a small script or imported in both component scripts) with one swap-in-place(url, selector) helper

findings.issue: In-memory cache Map is unbounded: expired entries are never evicted, only overwritten on re-request or deleted on error, so a long-lived server process visiting many move pages accumulates stale entries
findings.suggestion: Evict expired entries lazily on set (e.g. sweep entries when size exceeds a cap), or cap the Map with a simple LRU

findings.issue: API responses are typed as any throughout (also (a: any) casts in app/src/pages/pokemon/[name].astro:44-51 and app/src/pages/moves/[name].astro:16-18) despite tsconfig extending astro/tsconfigs/strict, so schema drift in the live API fails silently
findings.suggestion: Define interfaces for the PokeAPI payloads actually consumed (Species, Pokemon, Move, Type, Ability) in lib/api.ts and have getJson<T> call sites supply them

findings.issue: Server-side getJson uses bare fetch with no timeout; a hung upstream request blocks the page render indefinitely
findings.suggestion: Pass AbortSignal.timeout(...) (Node 24 platform API) to fetch, treating timeouts as errors/404s

findings.issue: Astro 7 made route caching stable (cache.provider + routeRules), which would absorb the per-keystroke full page renders triggered by the search input without any code
findings.suggestion: Optionally configure cache: { provider: memoryCache() } with routeRules for '/' to short-circuit repeated home-page renders while the upstream-data cache handles freshness

summary: This app targets Astro's current stable line (7.4.x) with only current, documented APIs, a two-dependency footprint, and a genuinely platform-first client layer that would survive a framework upgrade with almost no changes. Its forward-looking weaknesses are small and local: one raw process.env read where astro:env is now recommended, untyped PokeAPI payloads behind a strict tsconfig, a duplicated partial-navigation script, and an unbounded runtime cache. A capable PR I'd approve with nits.
